post.description:
Initiate graceful server shutdown.

Administrative shutdown is a receipt-bound lifecycle operation: it requires
both authenticated runtime control (the attach credential) and receipt
ownership (the lifecycle capability that discovery never references), so a
foreign attachment that can reach the product surface still cannot stop the
gateway.

Run admission is closed first, so the gateway admits no new run while it
drains; the in-process stop is then deferred briefly so this 202 flushes
before the owning Uvicorn server begins its deadline-bound connection drain
and application lifespan teardown.

post.description:
Start a run: resolve its agent, freeze it, create and dispatch in one call.

A repeat run id is a replay: the original run is returned when the request
is the same one, and refused when it is not. A selection the requested
provider's lane cannot apply exactly is a 422 whose body carries the stable
reason code and the values that would have been accepted.

``skills`` names skills the opening turn is given in full. A list that
repeats a name, names more than eight or names one of the wrong form is a
422 with the code ``skills_invalid``; on a service whose runs are accepted
with no skill it is ``skills_unavailable``; a name the run's skills lack is
``skill_not_found``. Each is refused before anything is started.

``attachments`` names files of the run's conversation the opening message
shares: the run's own id for a run that continues none, its predecessor's
conversation otherwise. A list that repeats a name, names more than 32 or
names one of the wrong form is a 422 ``attachments_invalid``; a name the
conversation lacks is a 404 ``attachment_not_found``; a file whose digest
is not the one sent is a 409 ``attachment_changed``. Each is refused
before anything is started.

``background`` starts the run as the host's background request, admitted
only with the host's own token in ``X-Host-Token`` (403
``background_not_admitted`` otherwise). Its agent is granted nothing, it
runs unattended, it is left out of the run listings, and its attachments
go into the model input. One that continues a run or asks for skills is a
422 ``background_request_invalid``; a lane that cannot run without tools a
422 ``background_lane_unsupported``; a document the lane cannot carry, or
one over the input bounds, a 422 ``input_not_supported``. A PDF input may
select its ``pages``, and a request reads at most 8 pages of a PDF: a
selection of more, or a PDF of more pages with none, is a 422
``document_pages_exceeded``, and a first page past the PDF's end a 422
``document_pages_out_of_range``, each naming the PDF's page count.

On a lane whose models run on this computer, a run whose first request
needs more context than its model is declared with is a 422
``model_does_not_fit``, whether or not the local server is running.
Otherwise the run's model is loaded before the run is created, at the
context its first request will ask for. A model the local server cannot
load with the memory this computer has free is a 422
``model_does_not_fit``; any other failed load a 422
``provider_unavailable``. Each leaves no run.

The default is the capped identity projection of durable non-terminal
runs: a caller that passes nothing sees exactly that.

``state=all`` is the history read, and it differs from discovery in more than
which rows it returns. It answers through the paginated list service rather
than the discovery one, because discovery exists to find live work and is
capped for that purpose while history has to walk a store that only grows;
that is why this mode carries a total and an offset. And it answers with a
WIDER record, because the two readings are asked different questions: a
viewer binding to live work needs an identity, while a reader of history is
asking what happened and needs the projection that separates a healthy run
from a degraded one.

The two shapes are returned as two models rather than one union, so widening
history cannot perturb a single byte of the certified discovery response.

get.description:
Read one run whole, including a terminal or archived one.

Distinct from run-status by design. Run-status is the BOUNDED recovery
snapshot a client reconciles authority from, and widening it would make
every reconciliation pay for a transcript it does not read. This is the
wide read for a consumer that wants the record: transcript, agents, plan,
pending answers, and the run's metadata.

"Whole" is a promise about honesty, not about always having everything. The
transcript lives only in the checkpoint, and a checkpoint can be gone or
unreachable; when it is, this answers 200 with the durable half of the
record it CAN read - status, agents, plan, permissions, metadata - and says
plainly that the transcript is not part of it. Refusing the whole read over
an absent transcript would cost the caller the half that survived, and
answering an unqualified empty message list would be worse still: silent
loss dressed as a run that never spoke.

The state snapshot is embedded rather than restated, so this response cannot
drift from the snapshot it reports.

The two durable artifacts this verb discloses that no other surface serves -
the settled permission decisions and the token accounting - are here for the
same reason: both were recorded on every run and readable nowhere, and
reporting the record is this verb's whole job.

post.description:
Queue a follow-up turn behind the one an existing run is executing.

A run that is still executing a turn (SUBMITTED, RUNNING) takes the
follow-up and answers 202 with ``action_status`` ``queued`` and the place
it was given. The turn is reserved in the run's journal and NOTHING else:
it binds no graph receipt, installs no writer and is not dispatched, which
is what keeps the executing turn's own terminal from being refused as
superseded. It becomes a dispatch only once that turn's terminal
checkpoint is proven, and the run stays RUNNING across the boundary.

A consumer must therefore not read a quiet turn boundary as completion: a
run holding a queued continuation emits no terminal frame at the end of
its first turn, and one at the end of its last.

One continuation waits per run, and the service bounds the total. A second
offer while one waits refuses ``queue_full``; nothing was reserved, and
the caller may offer again once the waiting turn has run.

Every other state still refuses, each for its own reason. A cancelling run
is leaving, so a turn queued behind it would wait for a promotion that can
never come. A parked run answers through its own typed respond verb, and a
message here would start a turn that orphans the pause. A settled run is
over; continuing it is a new run that names it as its predecessor.

Run-start cannot carry this. A repeat run identifier there is a REPLAY - it
answers with the original run and never adopts the new body - so without
this verb the versioned surface can start a run and watch it, but never say
anything further to it.

The caller names the turn. ``Idempotency-Key`` is required here and has no
server-derived default, because a default can only be derived from what the
request already says - the run, the agent, the text - and two deliberate
identical continuations are two turns, not one sent twice. Under a derived
key the second was answered as a replay of the first and never ran. A
request that names no key is refused before anything is read.

Queued is not applied: the turn has not started, so a caller reconciles
from the stream or run-status rather than from this response.

``skills`` names skills of the run the turn is given in full, kept with
the queued turn. A list that repeats a name, names more than eight or names
one of the wrong form is a 422 with the code ``skills_invalid``; for a run
accepted with no skill it is ``skills_unavailable``; a name the run's skills
lack is ``skill_not_found``. Nothing is reserved for a refused list.

``attachments`` names files of the run's conversation the turn shares,
each pinned now with its digest and type and kept with the queued turn. A
list that repeats a name, names more than 32 or names one of the wrong form
is a 422 ``attachments_invalid``; a name the conversation lacks is a 404
``attachment_not_found``; a file whose digest is not the one sent is a 409
``attachment_changed``. Nothing is reserved for a refused list.

post.description:
Answer a permission request the run raised on its progress stream.

The versioned surface POSES this question - ``permission_request`` is an
enumerated frame on run-stream - and this is where the answer returns. It
is the only answering channel, so without it every paused run would be
stranded.

The verb adds no state machine of its own: it is a versioned projection of
the same answer path, so at-most-once behaviour comes from there. Answering
twice replays the stored outcome rather than acting again, an answer arriving
after the request was applied reports the duplicate without re-dispatching,
and a superseded or expired request is refused with a journaled rejection
that replays identically.

Scoping matters as much as the answer. The service resolves the request
against the run in the path, from that run's live checkpoint, BEFORE anything
acts on it, so a guessed request id cannot be used to answer another run's
question - and a mismatch has no effect at all rather than being detected
after the fact.

get.description:
Top-level health check: the one probe surface for external callers.

In every profile the unauthenticated boundary discloses only the minimal
liveness fact - no process identity, product identity, filesystem layout,
worker state, or product state. A caller presenting the gateway bearer
additionally receives the detailed body: under the armed desktop profile
the readiness projection from the single readiness authority, computed
over a live database probe; under every other profile the probe
aggregate. Only the authenticated branch probes: the unauthenticated
answer stays a constant so it cannot be used to measure the gateway's
dependencies. A lifecycle caller needs nothing more from it, since an
answering ``200`` is its liveness test and the owner's pid is confirmed
on the authenticated service-state verb.

Both detailed bodies PROBE rather than read off app state - the DB here
and, on the development profile, the checkpointer and worker as well -
because a healthcheck that only reports what the process believes about
itself cannot notice a dependency that has gone away.

200.description: Every profile serves the minimal liveness fact to a caller without the gateway bearer. A bearer-authenticated caller receives the readiness projection under the armed desktop profile and the probe aggregate under every other profile.

AgentSnapshot.title: AgentSnapshot
AgentSnapshot.description:
The agent of a run, and what it is doing.

``state``, ``provider`` and ``effort`` are served as their enumerations, so
an unrecognised value never reaches the wire as an arbitrary string.

``model_name`` is free-form by contrast, and deliberately so: it is the exact
provider-issued catalog identifier the run executed, and a served catalog
names its own models, so no closed vocabulary could cover them. ``None`` for
an agent whose model was never resolved. ``effort`` is the effort level the
run's selection froze, ``None`` when none applies.

AgentSpec.title: AgentSpec

``model`` may be omitted when the operator configured a default model for

``workspace_root`` must be absolute; whether it exists and may be used is
the service's check, not this type's.

AuthKind.title: AuthKind
AuthKind.description:
What a host supplies for a lane to authenticate.

Values:
    API_KEY: A key, carried in the credential frame under the lane's
        ``agent_credential_id``. The lane has a declared endpoint; a
        ``base_url`` handed with the key replaces it.
    API_KEY_WITH_BASE_URL: A key and the vendor endpoint it is valid for.
        ``default_base_url`` is the endpoint used when none is handed; when
        it is null an endpoint must be handed with the key.
    PROVIDER_SIGN_IN_ONLY: Nothing. The lane's program authenticates from
        its own sign-in, and the credential frame carries nothing for it.
    NONE: Nothing. The lane reaches an unauthenticated server on this
        computer; the credential frame carries nothing for it.

BackgroundRequest.title: BackgroundRequest
BackgroundRequest.description:
What a host asks of a background request beyond the run's message.

Admitted only on the host's own token (``X-Host-Token``). ``system`` follows
the service's neutral instruction as the run's persona. ``max_output_tokens``
bounds the reply: a reply over it fails the run. ``deadline_seconds`` bounds
the run; omitted, the service's run limits apply.

``temperature`` (0 to 2) sets the sampling temperature, ``context_tokens``
(512 to 1,048,576) the size of the model's context window, and
``response_schema`` is a JSON Schema object (at most 32,768 bytes as compact
JSON) the model's reply is constrained to. The reply is still text: the
caller extracts and validates the JSON. A lane honours these options only
where its transport sends them to the model; a request that names an option
its lane does not honour is refused with ``background_option_unsupported``
instead of running with the option ignored. Omitted, the lane's own
behaviour applies.

The run's agent ``effort`` is a fourth such option: a background request
names one only on a lane whose served ``background_requests.options`` lists
``effort``, and only at a level its model offers. Named on any other lane,
it is refused with ``background_option_unsupported``.

proven it on this host: ``proven``, ``unproven_version`` or ``unproven``.

``entry`` names the tool-server entry the state is for. It is given exactly
for tool access and writing, the capabilities proven together with an
entry. ``generation`` names the models' multi-agent generation the state is
for, where the lane's proof covers some generations only; a frozen selection
keeps the state of its own model's generation.

The source must be a settled run of the same workspace whose conversation

ClarificationKind.title: ClarificationKind
ClarificationKind.description:
How one question is answered.

``choice`` offers a bounded set of declared options and admits exactly one of
them verbatim as its answer; ``text`` admits free prose up to
:data:`MAX_ANSWER_CHARS`. The two exhaust the vocabulary: a kind the renderer
does not know is a question it cannot render, so the set is closed.

ClarificationQuestion.title: ClarificationQuestion
ClarificationQuestion.description:
One bounded question inside a clarification request.

``options`` belongs to ``choice`` and only to ``choice``: a text question
carrying options would advertise a constraint the answer path does not
enforce, and a choice without options would offer nothing to choose. Both are
refused at construction rather than tolerated and interpreted downstream.

ClarificationRequest.title: ClarificationRequest
ClarificationRequest.description:
The bounded question set a parked run is waiting on.

This is the interrupt payload verbatim: what the node raises, what the
checkpoint holds while the run is parked, and what the recovery snapshot
discloses. ``type`` is carried rather than implied because the checkpoint
holds interrupts of several kinds side by side and the discriminator is how a
reader tells a clarification from an approval.

CleanupKind.title: CleanupKind

Deliberately a kind and never a locator: it names *what class of state* a
delete touched, so both the durable cleanup manifest and the delete
response can speak it, while the concrete checkpoint id or artifact path
stays inside the control plane.

ConversationCarry.title: ConversationCarry

A carry takes whole turns, newest first, within a budget of estimated

``omitted_tokens`` are the older turns that did not, which the new
conversation cannot read. ``limit`` is set only when the newest turn alone
was larger than the budget: ``receipts`` says its tool evidence was reduced
to receipts, ``cut`` that its text was cut at the budget as well.
``source_lane`` is the provider and transport, as ``provider/transport``,
that the earlier conversation's newest run used, when it recorded one.

ConversationLaneFixedRefusalDetail.title: ConversationLaneFixedRefusalDetail
ConversationLaneFixedRefusalDetail.description:
Why a continuing run was refused for naming another provider or transport.

A conversation stays on the provider and transport of its newest run.
``provider`` and ``transport`` name that lane, so a host can correct its
picker; another lane is reached only by starting a new conversation with
``carries_from_run_id``. Nothing was started and no other lane was
substituted.

ConversationLaneUnreadableRefusalDetail.title: ConversationLaneUnreadableRefusalDetail
ConversationLaneUnreadableRefusalDetail.description:
Why a continuing run was refused because its lane could not be read.

The run being continued holds a record of the provider and transport it
ran on, and the record cannot be read. The conversation's lane is then not
known, so no lane is chosen for it and none is allowed to change. Nothing
was started. A run stored before lanes were recorded holds no record and is
not refused.

ConversationTitleRefusalDetail.title: ConversationTitleRefusalDetail
ConversationTitleRefusalDetail.description:

``conversation_not_found``: no run has the id, or the run continues
another and so is not a conversation's root. ``title_invalid``: the title
is empty once stripped, or longer than 200 characters.

ConversationTitleRefusalResponse.title: ConversationTitleRefusalResponse

The title is stripped and must then be 1 to 200 characters; anything else
is refused with the code ``title_invalid``.

DeclaredBackground.title: DeclaredBackground
DeclaredBackground.description:

How far each is proven on a host is the served catalog's answer, not this
one's.

Attributes:
    runnable: Whether the lane runs a background request at all.
    inputs: The inputs the lane's transport carries in a background
        request's turn (``text``, ``image``, ``pdf``), in that order. Empty
        where the lane is not runnable. On a lane whose models differ, a
        model must also read the input: see each model's ``vision``.
    options: The run options the lane honours (``temperature``,
        ``context_tokens``, ``response_schema``, ``effort``), in that
        order. A request naming any other is refused. ``effort`` is named
        by the run's agent effort, at one of the levels the model's
        ``effort`` states.

DeclaredIconAttribution.description:

A client that shows the artwork shows it under these terms.

    url: Where the source is published.
    pin: The exact release the artwork was taken from.
    licence: The licence the drawings are used under.
    notice: The copyright and permission notice that licence requires.
    trademarks: The statement that the depicted marks are their holders'.

DeclaredIconVariant.description:

    media_type: The artwork's media type.
    sha256: The SHA-256 of the artwork's bytes, as lowercase hex. The

DeclaredLane.description:

Attributes:
    id: ``<provider>_<transport>``, stable and unique per lane.
    provider: The canonical provider id a run names. A string, not a
        closed set: a provider added to the build is a new entry, not a
        change of shape.
    transport: ``api`` or ``cli``.
    display_name: The provider's name as shown to a person. Every lane of a
        provider carries the same name.
    description: One sentence saying what the provider is, for a person
        choosing one. Every lane of a provider carries the same text.
    auth_kind: What a host supplies for the lane (:class:`AuthKind`).
    logout: Whether the hosted provider's sign-out command applies to this lane.
    default_base_url: The endpoint the lane uses when none is handed, or
        null when it declares none.
    agent_credential_id: The id the credential frame carries this lane's
        credential under, or null when the frame carries none for it.
    reads_off_host: Whether the lane sends a run's content to a computer
        other than this one. False only for a lane whose every endpoint is
        validated as loopback.
    cli_programs: The program names a CLI lane resolves on the search path;
        empty for an API lane.
    icon: The provider's icon, whose artwork the service bundles and
        serves for the client to draw, or null when it has none. Every lane
        of a provider carries the same icon.
    platform: The provider's public pages and endpoints: its
        documentation, its model-list endpoint and where it publishes its
        service status. Every lane of a provider carries the same value.
    default_model: The model the lane uses when a run names none, or null
        when the lane names none. When given it is one of ``models``.
    models: The models the lane offers, by id. Empty when no source lists
        any; the lane is still listed.
    recommended: The model the lane recommends for each capability
        (``vision``, ``text``), by capability. Empty where the lane
        recommends none; each value is one of ``models``.
    background: What a host's background request on the lane may carry.
    unread: The sources the metadata meant to read for the lane and did
        not, with the reason. A lane named here is described from the next
        source in order of authority, not from the vendor's own listing.

DeclaredLicence.title: DeclaredLicence
DeclaredLicence.description:
The licence a model is distributed under, without its text.

Attributes:
    spdx: The SPDX identifier, where the licence text is a recognised
        standard text; null otherwise.
    name: The licence's name as shown to a person.
    digest: ``sha256:`` and the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the licence text,
        as the vendor's registry names it.

DeclaredModel.title: DeclaredModel
DeclaredModel.description:
One model a lane offers, as the provider publishes it.

Attributes:
    id: The model id a run names, in the vendor's own spelling.
    display_name: The model's name as shown to a person.
    effort: Whether the model reasons and which effort levels it accepts on
        this lane. A model with no effort control is distinct from one whose
        effort control is unknown.
    vision: Whether the model accepts images, or null where no source states
        it.
    size_bytes: The model's download size in bytes, or null where no source
        states it.
    context_length: The model's context length in tokens, or null where no
        source states it.
    licence: The licence the model is distributed under, or null where no
        source states it. The licence text is not part of this document.
    artefacts: How each local engine obtains the model (what the host
        fetches), and the context a llama.cpp load of it asks for, or null
        where no source states it.

DeclaredProviderCatalog.title: DeclaredProviderCatalog
DeclaredProviderCatalog.description:
The declared document: its version and one entry per registered lane.

Attributes:
    schema_version: The version of the document's shape.
    providers: One entry per registered lane.
    icon_attribution: The terms the icon artwork the lanes name is used
        under.
    task_kinds: The kinds of task a host keys its background settings
        by, in a closed vocabulary.

DeclaredTaskKind.title: DeclaredTaskKind
DeclaredTaskKind.description:
One kind of task a host runs background requests for.

A background request does not name its kind: the host resolves the kind to
a lane, a model and an effort, and the request carries those.

Attributes:
    id: The value the kind is keyed by.
    display_name: The kind's name as shown to a person.
    description: One sentence saying what a task of the kind does.

DegradedReason.title: DegradedReason
DegradedReason.description:
Why a run snapshot is less than complete, in terms a program can match.

These are the machine-readable members of a run snapshot's degradation list.
They are deliberately NOT the same vocabulary as the service-state
degradation list, which carries human-readable prose ("worker is down") for
an operator to read rather than tokens for a client to branch on. The two
share a field name and nothing else, so they stay separate declarations.

Membership follows the reader's fault lines: what could not be read
(``*_UNAVAILABLE``, ``*_UNREADABLE``, ``*_TIMEOUT``), what was read but is
not current (``*_STALE``), what should have been present and was not
(``*_MISSING``), what was present but contradicts another store (the
permission residue and cross-store mismatch members), and what the read
PROVED but could not write (``*_CONTENDED``).

DesktopReadiness.title: DesktopReadiness
DesktopReadiness.description:
The authenticated desktop readiness projection.

Carries process and product identity alongside the five separate bounded
readiness facts. The facts are never collapsed into a single boolean: a cold,
startable worker leaves ``gateway_readiness`` ``ready`` while ``run_admission``
stays ``deferred`` or ``blocked``, so attachment and execution readiness
remain distinct. Served only to an attach-authenticated caller.

Effort.title: Effort
Effort.description:
How much reasoning a run asks its model for, lowest first.

The ordered union of the values the provider lanes offer. Every lane spells
the values it supports with these same strings, so a member's value is also
the provider-native value; what differs per lane is which members it
accepts and how the value reaches the provider.

EffortCapability.title: EffortCapability
EffortCapability.description:
Whether a model reasons, and the effort levels it accepts on its lane.

Attributes:
    reasoning: Whether the model reasons (:class:`Reasoning`).
    control: Whether it has effort levels, none, or none are known.
    levels: The accepted levels, lowest first; empty unless ``control``
        is ``levels``.
    default: The level applied when a run names none, or null when no
        vendor source states one.

EffortControl.title: EffortControl
EffortControl.description:
What a model's sources state about its effort control.

Values:
    LEVELS: It accepts the listed effort levels.
    NONE: It has no effort control.
    UNKNOWN: No source states a level set.

EngineDoor.title: EngineDoor
EngineDoor.description: Where a person goes to start or repair a local engine.

EngineDownReason.title: EngineDownReason
EngineDownReason.description:
Why a local engine's server could not be read, as a closed set.

Values:
    NO_ANSWER_IN_TIME: The server accepted the request and did not answer
        within the read's bound.
    NOT_REACHABLE: The connection could not be made or was lost.
    ANSWER_UNREADABLE: The server answered, but not in the shape this
        engine's server documents.

EngineHealthResponse.title: EngineHealthResponse
EngineHealthResponse.description: Whether a local engine's server runs, with the reason and door when not.

EngineState.title: EngineState
EngineState.description: Whether a local engine's server answered the read of it.

ExecutionTaskSnapshot.title: ExecutionTaskSnapshot
ExecutionTaskSnapshot.description:
Normalized execution task used in reconnect snapshots.

The one declaration of an execution task: the worker emits it across the
gateway-worker wire, the gateway persists it, and the snapshot serves it.

FrozenNativeControlSummary.title: FrozenNativeControlSummary
FrozenNativeControlSummary.description: One exact provider-native value frozen for historical disclosure.

FrozenSelectionSummary.title: FrozenSelectionSummary
FrozenSelectionSummary.description:
The immutable execution authority a run was frozen with.

Names the exact served catalog entry and provider-native inputs the run
executes under, how far its lane had been proven on this host when the run
started, whether the hosted package had completed a qualifying turn, and
how far each capability had been. ``capability_proofs`` states
tool access and writing for each tool server the run names, which is the
proof state of what the run mounts, and then web retrieval, reading an
image and reading a PDF. A run frozen before these states were recorded
lists none.

GatewayHealthResponse.title: GatewayHealthResponse
GatewayHealthResponse.description:
The unarmed profile's probe body on ``GET /health``, served on the bearer.

A caller without the gateway bearer receives the minimal liveness body
instead. Declared because it was published as an untyped object: a reader
of the contract learned no field name, no status vocabulary, and no way to
tell this body from the minimal liveness one.

Open on purpose. The fields below are the ones the endpoint itself
guarantees on every answer, including the degraded answer it gives when a
runtime singleton is missing; the probe aggregate carries further
dependency checks whose set depends on what this build probes, and
publishing them as a closed shape would promise a client a stability the
aggregate does not have. ``additionalProperties`` says so rather than
leaving the whole body unnamed.

GatewayReadiness.title: GatewayReadiness
GatewayReadiness.description:
Whether a live gateway with a valid database is ready to be attached.

Independent of worker state: a live gateway with a valid database and a cold,
startable worker is ``ready``. A gateway-owned dependency failure - an invalid
or unreachable database - is ``not_ready``.

HealthState.title: HealthState
HealthState.description: A factual binary health axis whose evidence may still be unknown.

HostProgram.title: HostProgram
HostProgram.description: One program the host declares and a run may start.

HostToolServer.title: HostToolServer
HostToolServer.description: One stdio tool server the host declares and the service gives every run.

HostToolsDisclosure.title: HostToolsDisclosure
HostToolsDisclosure.description:
The tools the host declares, as the service gives them to its runs.

The host declares them in the gateway's launch environment and the gateway
reads them once, when it starts. Both lists are in name order, and both are
empty where the service gives its runs no host tools: it mounts tool servers
only beside the hosted root or with the development tool server on, and
elsewhere a declaration is validated and unused.

HostToolsNotice.title: HostToolsNotice
HostToolsNotice.description:
What a service says when its host declares fewer kinds of tool than two.

A host declares tool servers and programs. A service whose host declares
neither starts all the same and says so, in the service answer and in its
start-up log. One whose host declares a single kind says which kind its
runs lack. No notice is served when the host declares both kinds, or when
the service gives its runs no host tools at all.

HostedCertificationState.title: HostedCertificationState
HostedCertificationState.description: Whether a lane has a current turn through the shipped hosted package.

HuggingFaceArtefact.title: HuggingFaceArtefact
HuggingFaceArtefact.description:
A GGUF model, and its projector, at one commit of a Hugging Face repository.

Attributes:
    source: ``huggingface``.
    repository: ``<owner>/<repo>``, each a plain name.
    revision: The full lowercase commit id the files are fetched at; never
        a branch or tag, so the pinned digests keep describing the bytes.
    model: The GGUF model file.
    projector: The projector file the model loads with to read images, or
        null for a model without one; left out of the document then. It is
        never the model file itself.

IconVariant.title: IconVariant
IconVariant.description:
How an icon is drawn.

Values:
    MONO: One colour, ``currentColor``, so it follows the client's text.
    COLOR: The brand's own colours.

LaneCapability.title: LaneCapability
LaneCapability.description:
A capability whose proof state a lane discloses. The value is the wire form.

Web retrieval is withheld from a lane that has not proven it. Tool access
and writing through this service's own tool server are never withheld:
each call is put to the person, so their state is disclosed only. Reading
an image and reading a PDF cannot be withheld, so their state is a claim
only: what the service may say the lane does.

LaneStatus.title: LaneStatus
LaneStatus.description: One lane's service state, from the components mapped to it.

LaneVerification.title: LaneVerification
LaneVerification.description:
How far a lane, or one capability on it, had been proven on this host.

For the lane itself the work is a completed turn; for a capability it is the
work that capability's own live test completed.

ListingCheck.title: ListingCheck
ListingCheck.description:
The result of comparing one lane's live listing with the document.

The comparison reads the lane's own model listing and sends no prompt.
It carries no proof field and grants, implies or withdraws no proof.

Attributes:
    provider: The canonical provider id.
    transport: The lane's transport.
    checked_at: When the listing was read, in UTC.
    no_verdict: Why no comparison was made, or null when one was.
    detail: A person-readable account of a missing verdict.
    findings: Every difference found, by model then drift.

ListingDrift.title: ListingDrift
ListingDrift.description:
How a lane's live listing differs from the packaged document.

Values:
    MODEL_MISSING_LIVE: A packaged model is absent from the live listing.
    MODEL_NEW_LIVE: The live listing has a model the document lacks.
    EFFORT_SET_MISMATCH: The live effort levels differ from the packaged.
    DEFAULT_MISMATCH: The live default effort differs from the packaged.

ListingFinding.title: ListingFinding
ListingFinding.description:
One difference between a live listing and the packaged document.

Level and default values are in the listing's own spelling. Levels are
present only on an effort-set mismatch, defaults only on a default mismatch.

LivenessResponse.title: LivenessResponse
LivenessResponse.description:
The unauthenticated liveness body.

Deliberately minimal: it carries only the liveness fact and discloses no
process identity, product identity, or product state. An unauthenticated
caller of the gateway, in every profile, observes this and nothing more.

LivenessState.title: LivenessState
LivenessState.description:
Minimal process-liveness fact: the gateway answered, or it did not.

This is the only fact an unauthenticated caller ever observes. It proves
neither ownership nor readiness and discloses no product state.

LocalEngine.title: LocalEngine
LocalEngine.description: A keyless engine whose server runs on this computer.

carried_from_run_id.title: Carried From Run Id
carried_from_run_id.description: The run whose conversation this message was carried from, when it entered this conversation as carried text of an earlier one; null for a message said in this conversation. Its timestamp is then when it was first said, not when it was carried.

MessageSnapshot.title: MessageSnapshot
MessageSnapshot.description: Fully materialized message in a thread replay.

ModelArtefacts.title: ModelArtefacts
ModelArtefacts.description:
How each local engine obtains one model.

Each engine's artefact is null where the catalog declares no way to obtain
the model for that engine.

Attributes:
    ollama: The registry name the Ollama engine pulls the model as.
    llamacpp: What the llama.cpp engine fetches: a registry name, whose
        manifest carries a projector layer where the model reads images, or
        a Hugging Face model with its projector.
    llamacpp_default_context: The context size, in tokens, a llama.cpp load of
        the model asks for, or null where none is declared. It never exceeds
        :data:`LLAMACPP_CONTEXT_CEILING` or the model's context length, and
        is declared only with a llama.cpp artefact.

ModelDeletedResponse.title: ModelDeletedResponse
ModelDeletedResponse.description: A model removed from this computer.

ModelLicenceResponse.title: ModelLicenceResponse
ModelLicenceResponse.description:
One model's licence, as its lane's catalog states it, with the text.

``spdx``, ``name`` and ``digest`` are the catalog entry's ``licence``;
``digest`` is ``sha256:`` and the hex SHA-256 of ``text`` encoded as UTF-8.
``installed`` is the entry's own.

ModelListSource.title: ModelListSource
ModelListSource.description:
Where a lane's model list was read from.

Values:
    ACCOUNT: The signed-in account's own listing, read in the person's
        provider home. It decides which models the lane offers.
    PACKAGED: The document this service ships. A lane whose runtime
        publishes an account listing serves it when the listing could not
        be read, or while it is still being read, so a host can say that
        the account's list is not the one in view.

ModelPullFailure.title: ModelPullFailure
ModelPullFailure.description:
Why a pull failed.

``code`` is ``model_pull_stalled`` when the server sent no progress for a
minute, ``model_pull_refused`` when it refused the pull or ended it early,
and ``provider_unavailable`` when it could not be reached.

model.title: Model
model.description: The model, as it was asked for.

status.title: Status
status.description: The server's last status text, on one line.

finished_at.title: Finished At
finished_at.description: When the pull ended; null while it runs.

ModelPullResponse.title: ModelPullResponse
ModelPullResponse.description:
One pull at one moment, whole.

``completed_bytes`` and ``total_bytes`` sum over the layers the server has
named so far, so the total can grow while a pull is running; both are null
until the server names a layer.

ModelRefusalDetail.title: ModelRefusalDetail
ModelRefusalDetail.description:
Why a model management request was refused.

``code`` is one of ``unknown_lane``, ``model_management_unsupported``,
``model_name_invalid``, ``model_pull_unknown``, ``model_pulls_busy``,
``model_not_installed``, ``model_pull_running`` and ``provider_unavailable``.

ModelRefusalResponse.title: ModelRefusalResponse
ModelRefusalResponse.description: The body of a refused model management request.

MultiAgentGeneration.title: MultiAgentGeneration
MultiAgentGeneration.description:
The multi-agent runtime a model runs its native subagents on.

A lane whose models differ here bounds their subagents differently: on
Codex, a ``v1`` model's children are held to one level by the lane's own
configuration, while a ``v2`` model spawns at any depth whatever it says.

Values:
    DISABLED: The model runs no native subagents.
    V1: The first runtime, whose depth the lane's configuration bounds.
    V2: The second runtime, whose depth no configuration bounds.

NoVerdictReason.title: NoVerdictReason
NoVerdictReason.description: Why a listing comparison reached no verdict.

count.title: Count
count.description: How many consecutive pages from it.

PageSelection.title: PageSelection
PageSelection.description:
The pages of a PDF that a background request's input asks for.

*first* is the first page, counted from 1, and *count* how many consecutive
pages to read from it. A request reads one window of pages of a PDF. A
*count* over that, or a *first* past the document's end, is not a form
error: it is refused with a code of its own once the document is read.

PermissionOptionKind.title: PermissionOptionKind
PermissionOptionKind.description:
The answers a person can give one tool-permission request.

There is no answer that outlives the session: nothing is remembered for a
later session, and a provider's own "always" option is never offered or
chosen.

Values:
    ALLOW_ONCE: Allow this call only; the next call is asked again.
    ALLOW_SESSION: Allow this call and, for the rest of this session, every
        later call the same grant covers, without asking again.
    REJECT_ONCE: Refuse this call.

tool_name.title: Tool Name
tool_name.description: The bare name of the tool the request is about within its server, e.g. 'authority'. Null when the request names no tool.

tool_reach.description: How far the tool reaches: 'local_read' reads this machine, 'local_write' may change it, 'online' may reach beyond it. Null when it is not known.

PermissionSnapshot.title: PermissionSnapshot
PermissionSnapshot.description: Outstanding permission request in a state snapshot.

PlanEntry.title: PlanEntry
PlanEntry.description:
A single entry in the agent's execution plan.

Fields use plain ``str`` so the domain layer stays free of wire-protocol
enum imports.  Values follow the ACP plan-entry vocabularies: status
``pending`` / ``in_progress`` / ``completed``, priority ``high`` / ``medium``
/ ``low``.

PlatformUrls.title: PlatformUrls
PlatformUrls.description:
A provider's public pages and endpoints.

Attributes:
    docs_url: The vendor documentation the lanes were configured from.
    models_url: The vendor's model-list endpoint, where one is published.
    status: Where the vendor publishes its service status.

ProgramStart.title: ProgramStart
ProgramStart.description:
What one program start would run: the program, its arguments, and where.

Attributes:
    executable: The path of the program that would be started.
    arguments: Every argument it would be started with, in order. Their
        characters together are bounded too, at the figure the run stream
        publishes for the same list.
    working_directory: The directory it would start in: the run's workspace.

Provider.title: Provider
Provider.description: Canonical product identities shared by requests and configuration.

ProviderCatalogResponse.title: ProviderCatalogResponse
ProviderCatalogResponse.description:
The served provider catalog: one record per lane, and the task kinds.

``task_kinds`` is the closed vocabulary of kinds of background task, each
with a name and a sentence to show a person, so a host can key a setting
per kind without keeping a list of its own. A background request does not
name a kind: the host resolves its kind to a lane, a model and an effort,
and the request carries those.

ProviderCondition.title: ProviderCondition
ProviderCondition.description:
Why a provider failed, in terms a client can act on.

The value is the wire form: lowercase, underscore-separated, and stable.

ProviderEligibility.title: ProviderEligibility
ProviderEligibility.description:
Whether at least one subprocess provider may be served work on this host.

Decided by lane admission, which requires a recorded completed-turn proof
for the lane, a resolved launcher whose reported version that proof admits,
and the lane's own readiness - its configuration present and its launch
command resolvable. All three, conjunctively.

Credential readiness is NECESSARY and never SUFFICIENT: a lane whose
credential resolves and whose launcher is installed is still ``ineligible``
until a live test has completed a real turn on it. An eligibility that
stopped at the credential served lanes with handshake coverage only, which
is the whole reason the proof term exists. No provider is constructed to
decide this, and the launcher's version report is cached per launch identity.

ProviderStatusReport.title: ProviderStatusReport
ProviderStatusReport.description:
A provider's service status as last read from the vendor.

Status is display and readiness information only. It never changes
whether a lane is selectable, admitted or proven, and never refuses a run.

Attributes:
    provider: The canonical provider id.
    status: The provider's overall state.
    lanes: Each registered lane's state, by transport.
    page_url: The status page a person reads, where there is one.
    checked_at: When the last successful read happened, or null if none has.
    incidents: Recent incidents the vendor lists, for display.
    failure: The last failed refresh since that read, if any.

ProviderStatusResponse.title: ProviderStatusResponse
ProviderStatusResponse.description: Every provider's last-read service status, by provider id.

ProviderTransport.title: ProviderTransport
ProviderTransport.description: How a run reaches a named provider product.

ProviderVerifyRequest.title: ProviderVerifyRequest
ProviderVerifyRequest.description: Name one exact lane; a provider with two transports must choose one.

ProviderVerifyResponse.title: ProviderVerifyResponse
ProviderVerifyResponse.description: A listing comparison tied to the packaged metadata revision.

model.title: Model
model.description: The model to pull: an Ollama reference of lowercase name segments separated by '/' and an optional ':tag', in at most 200 characters. Any other value is refused as model_name_invalid. Any model the server's library holds may be pulled, not only the lane's recommended ones.

PullModelRequest.title: PullModelRequest
PullModelRequest.description: A request to pull a model onto this computer.

Reasoning.title: Reasoning
Reasoning.description:
Whether a model reasons or thinks before it answers.

Values:
    SUPPORTED: It reasons; its sources state no on-off control.
    ALWAYS_ON: It always reasons and cannot be told not to.
    TOGGLE: Reasoning can be switched on and off.
    UNSUPPORTED: It does not reason.
    UNKNOWN: No source states it.

RegistryArtefact.title: RegistryArtefact
RegistryArtefact.description:
A model the Ollama model registry serves.

Attributes:
    source: ``registry``.
    name: The name the registry serves the model under,
        ``[[host/]namespace/]model[:tag]``.

ReleaseRefusal.title: ReleaseRefusal
ReleaseRefusal.description:
Why the host records a refusal of a read where it would release one.

The window can only allow or decline; a host whose installation or profile
policy keeps a file on this computer decides without asking. A refusal
tells the model what is true, so it does not wait for a request that will
not come.

RepairStatus.title: RepairStatus
RepairStatus.description:
Repair and readiness classification distinct from lifecycle.

Types ``threads.repair_status``, the durable answer to what is wrong with a
run. A run's served ``execution_readiness`` asks whether it is fit to resume
and answers from this same closed set, because it is derived from that repair
posture at read time rather than judged on its own; a new member is available
to both at once and neither can drift into a private vocabulary.

RunAdmission.title: RunAdmission
RunAdmission.description:
Whether the gateway would admit a run right now - the execution-ready fact.

``ready`` means execution-ready: a reachable worker and a provider this host
may be served, so this gate and the admission gate launch applies agree,
rather than admitting a run that the latter then refuses.
``deferred`` means gateway-ready but not yet execution-ready - the worker is
cold or starting and will start on demand. It is informational on the
readiness surface.
``blocked`` means a hard dependency or the profile's required native
execution isolation is unavailable. Attachment can remain gateway-ready.

RunAgentSelection.title: RunAgentSelection
RunAgentSelection.description: The provider, model and effort a run executes under.

RunArchiveResponse.title: RunArchiveResponse
RunArchiveResponse.description: Acknowledge a run moved to the archived state.

RunClarificationRespondRequest.title: RunClarificationRespondRequest
RunClarificationRespondRequest.description:
Resolve a parked questionnaire with answers, a new prompt, or a decline.

Carries exactly one outcome: answers keyed by question id, a new
prompt that continues the same run, or a payload-free decline that lets the
run proceed with no answer given. The questions themselves were disclosed
authoritatively by ``run-status``; the run id and request id address the
questionnaire from the path, so no outcome restates what was asked.

All bounds are imported from the domain contract rather than restated. The
checks that need the parked questions in hand (an id nobody asked about, a
required question left blank, a choice outside its declared options) are
applied only to the answer outcome by the route against the checkpoint; a
decline deliberately bypasses them because refusal is not an answer.

``decline`` admits only the literal ``true``: ``false`` would be a client
saying "not declining" while supplying no other outcome, which is a
contradiction better refused at the schema than interpreted.

RunClarificationRespondResponse.title: RunClarificationRespondResponse
RunClarificationRespondResponse.description:
Report the durable outcome of a questionnaire resolution.

Identical retries replay the journal outcome without dispatch while a lease
is fresh. ``applied`` becomes true only after the request-scoped checkpoint
receipt matches the accepted resolution fingerprint, including when a retry
follows a lost response after the graph already advanced.

RunDeleteResponse.title: RunDeleteResponse
RunDeleteResponse.description:
Report a deletion that finalized over state no pass could remove.

Carried only on that one outcome. A clean deletion answers with no body at
all, so the presence of this body IS the signal that external state was
stranded. Names the KINDS of item left behind and nothing more: a concrete
checkpoint id or artifact path is control-plane state and never the
caller's to receive.

RunHistoryResponse.title: RunHistoryResponse
RunHistoryResponse.description:
The full read of one run, including terminal and archived ones.

Deliberately distinct from run-status, which is the BOUNDED recovery
snapshot a client reconciles from. This is the wide read - transcript,
agents, plan, pending answers, and the run's metadata - for a consumer that
wants the whole record rather than the authority fields.

The state snapshot is embedded by reference rather than restated field by
field, so the two cannot drift apart as the snapshot evolves.

The transcript is the one part of the record this verb cannot always
deliver, because it lives only in the checkpoint. ``transcript_available``
and ``transcript_status`` say so outright, so ``state.messages`` is never
read as "this run had no conversation" when the truth is that its
conversation could not be read. They are the transcript's counterpart to the
snapshot's own ``snapshot_complete`` / ``degraded_reasons`` pairing.

``permission_decisions`` is the settled counterpart to the snapshot's PENDING
permissions. A gate leaves the pending list the moment it is answered or the
run ends, so this is where the record of a decision a human actually made is
readable: without it a run read whole would show no trace that anyone had
approved anything.

``usage`` is the run's token accounting, the same kind of disclosure: the
counts are recorded on every turn and this is the surface that serves them.
It is ``null`` when the run recorded no accounting rows, rather than a
zeroed object a reader would take for a run that spent nothing.
Run-status stays the bounded recovery snapshot and carries none of
this, so counts are a cost of the wide read by design.

RunLiveRefusalDetail.title: RunLiveRefusalDetail
RunLiveRefusalDetail.description:
Why a run start was refused while another run is live.

A service that allows one live run at a time refuses a start, rather than
queueing it, until the live run has settled. ``live_run_id`` names that run,
so a caller can offer to wait for it or to cancel it.

RunMessageRefusalCode.title: RunMessageRefusalCode
RunMessageRefusalCode.description:
The conditions a run action can be refused for.

A closed subset of the typed refusal vocabulary, so the published contract
names only what a refusal can carry rather than every failure the gateway
knows. Each value is spelled as its failure-type counterpart.

Shared by every verb that reaches the worker through a run dispatch, not
only the follow-up turn: the same worker refusal must mean the same thing
whichever verb met it, so a client branches on one code set for every verb.

RunMessageRefusalDetail.title: RunMessageRefusalDetail
RunMessageRefusalDetail.description:
Why a follow-up turn was refused, in terms a program can match.

The refusals this verb can raise are several distinct conditions sharing one
status code, and a prose message is the wrong place for a consumer to learn
which one it met. ``code`` is the closed refusal vocabulary; ``message`` is
the same sentence an operator reads. A refused follow-up changed nothing, so
the consumer's next move is always to re-read run-status rather than to
reconcile from this body.

RunMessageRefusalResponse.title: RunMessageRefusalResponse
RunMessageRefusalResponse.description: The body served for a refused follow-up turn.

skills.title: Skills
skills.description: Skills of the run, by name, whose full text this message's turn is given, as if the agent had loaded each one: 1 to 8 distinct names of the form cadrumo-<lowercase words>. Omitted or empty for none.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.description: Files of the run's conversation this message shares, by name: 1 to 32 distinct names of files uploaded to the conversation. Each is pinned with the digest and type it has when the message is accepted. Omitted or empty for none.

RunMessageRequest.title: RunMessageRequest
RunMessageRequest.description:
Send a follow-up turn into a run that already exists.

Run-start cannot express this: a repeat run identifier is a REPLAY, answered
with the original run, so there is no way to say "same run, new input"
through it. This is that verb.

RunMessageResponse.title: RunMessageResponse
RunMessageResponse.description:
Acknowledge a follow-up turn as queued behind the run's current turn.

Acceptance is not execution and it is not even dispatch: the turn is
reserved in the run's journal with a place in its queue, and it reaches
the worker only once the turn now running has proven its terminal
checkpoint. A caller reconciles progress from the stream or run-status,
never from this body.

``queue_position`` is where this turn sits, counting from one, and it is
stable across a replay of the same key: a caller that lost this response
and retried reads the same place rather than a new one. ``None`` only for
a response that reserved nothing.

``idempotency_key`` is the caller's own key echoed back, never a derived
one, because this verb has no default to derive: it is required on the
request, so an accepted turn always has a key and it is always the one the
caller chose.

RunMetadataInput.title: RunMetadataInput
RunMetadataInput.description: Caller-supplied provenance for a run: how it is named and where it came from.

RunPermissionDecision.title: RunPermissionDecision
RunPermissionDecision.description:
One permission decision this run settled, as the audit log recorded it.

Answers which tool call was approved or refused, with which option, and when.
Carries no tool INPUT and no prompt text, so a caller reviewing what a run was
permitted to do never has to read what it was asked to do.

RunPermissionRefusalResponse.title: RunPermissionRefusalResponse
RunPermissionRefusalResponse.description:
The body served when a permission answer is refused with a conflict.

Two shapes, deliberately stated as one union rather than as one shape the
verb does not always serve. A worker that refused the dispatch is reported
with the typed refusal every run action shares, because the condition is
the dispatch outcome and a consumer must be able to tell a busy run from a
request it should never send again. The guards this verb applies before
anything is dispatched - an answer to a request that is no longer pending,
an option the request never offered, a key already bound to a different
answer - carry a plain sentence, because they are conditions of this
request rather than of reaching the worker.

RunPermissionRespondRequest.title: RunPermissionRespondRequest
RunPermissionRespondRequest.description:
Answer one permission request raised by a run.

Carries the chosen option and, optionally, a reviewer comment. The options
themselves were advertised on the versioned progress stream in the
``permission_request`` frame that raised the question, so the answer names
one rather than restating it. ``notes`` is journaled with the accepted
answer and is part of its body: the same option sent again with a different
comment conflicts with the answer already accepted. The run resumes on the
chosen option alone.

RunPermissionRespondResponse.title: RunPermissionRespondResponse
RunPermissionRespondResponse.description:
Report what an answer did, including when it did nothing.

``accepted`` says the answer was taken; ``applied`` reports whether the
worker had durably confirmed applying this request's resolution when this
response was assembled - never whether THIS call resumed the run. A first
accepted answer therefore returns ``applied`` false with ``action_status``
``accepted_not_applied``: the resume is dispatched and application is
confirmed asynchronously. A duplicate replays the stored outcome rather
than acting twice - byte-identical to the first response until that
confirmation lands, ``applied`` true after it - so a caller retrying after
a lost response learns the current outcome instead of re-answering. An
answer arriving after the request was already applied reports ``accepted``
with ``applied`` true and ``action_status`` ``duplicate``.

RunReplyResponse.title: RunReplyResponse
RunReplyResponse.description:
A run's final reply, and what produced it.

``reply`` is the text of the last thing the run's agent said, once the run
has settled; ``None`` before that, or when the run ended without saying
anything. ``provider``, ``transport``, ``model`` and ``effort`` are the
lane the run was frozen with, ``None`` when its stored selection cannot be
read; ``agent_version`` is this service's version. ``provider_condition``
is why the run's provider failed, typed as on the run status; ``None``
unless the run failed with one.

RunStartRefusalResponse.title: RunStartRefusalResponse
RunStartRefusalResponse.description:
The typed body of a 409 that refused a run start before any run existed.

The refusals of a start that cannot be told apart by status. Any other 409
of this verb carries a plain sentence, or the shared dispatch refusal.

carries_from_run_id.title: Carries From Run Id
carries_from_run_id.description: Start a new conversation seeded with a bounded text carry of the conversation of this settled run, which must belong to the same workspace. The carry takes whole turns, newest first, within the service's token and turn budget, and the response's carry field discloses what was taken and what was left out. The source conversation is left unchanged. It cannot be combined with continues_run_id: a conversation stays on one provider and transport, and another lane is reached only by this field.

acknowledge_selection_change.title: Acknowledge Selection Change
acknowledge_selection_change.description: Accept, for this one run, a model or effort that differs from the run it continues. Without it such a start is refused with the code selection_change_unacknowledged, which discloses the cost. It applies only to a run that continues another, covers only this run and is never remembered.

skills.title: Skills
skills.description: Skills of the run, by name, whose full text this message's turn is given, as if the agent had loaded each one: 1 to 8 distinct names of the form cadrumo-<lowercase words>. Omitted or empty for none.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.description: Files of the run's conversation this message shares, by name: 1 to 32 distinct names of files uploaded to the conversation. Each is pinned with the digest and type it has when the message is accepted. Omitted or empty for none.

background.description: Start the run as a background request: no tools, no permission prompt, no place in the run listings, and the attached images and PDFs put into the model input. Admitted only with the host's own token in the X-Host-Token header.

RunStartRequest.title: RunStartRequest
RunStartRequest.description:
Start a run: the client-facing shape of thread-create + first message.

Names the agent that runs it (provider, model, effort and the workspace it
works in) and the opening message. The gateway threads this onto the same
dispatch path the internal thread-create flow uses - no second code path.

RunStartResponse.title: RunStartResponse
RunStartResponse.description: Acknowledge a started run, with its initial semantic status.

RunStatusResponse.title: RunStatusResponse
RunStatusResponse.description:
The authoritative recovery snapshot for a run.

Designed as the read a restarted agent service resumes or reports a run from:
the run's lifecycle and repair posture, the agent it executes under, and the
checkpoint cursor. Non-authoritative SSE progress frames may be lost freely;
this snapshot is the source of truth.

Every relay frame is droppable, so this response is where a reloading client
with no live stream recovers the run's failure condition, its queue depth and
the question it is parked on.

RunSubagentCancelResponse.title: RunSubagentCancelResponse
RunSubagentCancelResponse.description:
One subagent of a run's agent is stopped; the run goes on.

Repeating the request once it took effect answers the same, read from the
subagent's recorded ``cancelled`` state.

RunSubagentResponse.title: RunSubagentResponse
RunSubagentResponse.description:
One subagent of a run's agent, and what it did.

``tool_calls`` are the run's tool calls this subagent made, and
``pending_permissions`` the run's outstanding requests it raised; both are
answered and controlled through the run's own verbs, exactly as the agent's.

RunSubagentsResponse.title: RunSubagentsResponse
RunSubagentsResponse.description:
The subagents of a run's agent, in the order they started.

A subagent is activity of the run's one agent, nested under the tool call
that started it (``parent_tool_call_id``); it is not a run of its own.

RunSummariesResponse.title: RunSummariesResponse
RunSummariesResponse.description:
The history reading of the run listing.

Answers ``state=all`` only. The default reading keeps
:class:`ActiveRunsResponse` and its narrower record, so widening what history
reports cannot disturb the certified discovery shape.

``total`` is not optional here: this reading walks the paginated store and
always knows how many runs matched, which is what makes paging honest.

RunSummaryRecord.title: RunSummaryRecord
RunSummaryRecord.description:
One run as the history reading reports it: identity plus its projection.

Deliberately wider than :class:`ActiveRunRecord`, and deliberately a
SEPARATE model rather than fields added to it. Discovery answers the narrow
question "which runs are live, and where do I bind a viewer" and its shape is
certified byte-for-byte; a reader of history is asking what happened, and
needs the facts that distinguish a healthy run from a degraded one.

Every field here is one the list service already resolves - the degradation
projections in particular are its reading of checkpoint authority, not a
restatement of stored columns - so nothing is invented that the projection
cannot fill.

``conversation_id`` and ``title`` mean what they mean on
:class:`ActiveRunRecord`: the chain's root run and the conversation's
title, the same for every run of the chain.

RunTokenUsage.title: RunTokenUsage
RunTokenUsage.description:
Token counts a run's provider lanes reported, summed as recorded.

Counts, and only counts a lane actually declared. Nothing here is priced or
derived: no served lane is metered per token and the project holds no rate
table, so a cost field could only ever carry a number nobody measured.

``input_tokens`` and ``output_tokens`` are the two counts every lane
reports. The other three are the breakdown a lane may or may not report,
and they are ``null`` when no recorded turn reported them - which is a
different fact from a measured zero and is served as a different value.

SeededHistory.title: SeededHistory
SeededHistory.description:
The history a continuing run reads uncached, as the service estimates it.

``retained_messages`` enter the run's prompt and ``estimated_tokens`` is
their size by the same estimator the context budget uses, not a provider
tokenizer. ``omitted_messages`` older ones stay reachable only through the
conversation history tool.

SelectedModel.title: SelectedModel
SelectedModel.description: One model and effort, as a run was frozen with them or asked for them.

SelectionChangeUnacknowledgedRefusalDeta.title: SelectionChangeUnacknowledgedRefusalDetail
SelectionChangeUnacknowledgedRefusalDeta.description:
Why a continuing run that changes model or effort was refused.

Any change of model or effort makes the next request read the whole
retained history uncached. ``previous`` is what the run being continued
used, ``requested`` what this start asked for, and ``history`` the size of
the history the new model would read. Sending the same start with
``acknowledge_selection_change: true`` accepts the change for that one run.

SemanticPhase.title: SemanticPhase
SemanticPhase.description:
What a run is product-visibly doing, in terms that name no graph node.

The one vocabulary for a run's semantic position, served on run-status as
``semantic_phase``, on the run-start acknowledgement as ``semantic_status``,
and stamped onto progress frames. A run that has not dispatched is
``STARTING``; one that is executing is ``RUNNING``. The terminal members
collapse the lifecycle pairs a product reader cannot act on separately: an
archived run reads ``COMPLETED`` and a cancelling one reads ``CANCELLED``,
because the distinction is a lifecycle fact and this vocabulary is a
product one.

``RECOVERY_REQUIRED`` is the only member that is not a position: it says the
run cannot advance until it is repaired, which is what a reader needs before
any phase detail matters.

ServiceStateResponse.title: ServiceStateResponse
ServiceStateResponse.description:
Backend-served readiness for the agent service (service-state verb).

Distinguishes three truths a client must not conflate: the process is
``alive`` (it answered), the service ``can_accept_run`` (dependencies are
ready), and - separately, via the provider catalog - whether a chosen
provider is selectable. A live HTTP process is not evidence that a run can
start, so ``status`` is derived from real dependency probes rather than
hardcoded.

ServiceStatus.title: ServiceStatus
ServiceStatus.description: A provider's or lane's service state, as the vendor states it.

pages.description: For a PDF in a background request's input, the pages it selects.

SharedAttachment.title: SharedAttachment
SharedAttachment.description: One file shared with a message, as it stood when the turn was accepted.

sha256.title: Sha256
sha256.description: The lowercase hex SHA-256 the file is expected to have; the message is refused with attachment_changed when the stored file has another.

pages.description: For a PDF input of a background request: the pages to read, as 'first' (counted from 1) and 'count'. Omitted, the input means every page. A request reads at most 8 pages of a PDF: a selection of more, or a PDF of more pages with no selection, is refused with document_pages_exceeded, and a 'first' past the end with document_pages_out_of_range. Send one request per window of pages. Refused as attachments_invalid on any other file or request.

SharedAttachmentReference.title: SharedAttachmentReference
SharedAttachmentReference.description: One file of the run's conversation a message shares, by name.

applies_when.title: Applies When
applies_when.description: The skill's parsed selection predicate, without the keys it leaves unset; null when it declares none.

files.title: Files
files.description: Every file of the skill, SKILL.md included, in path order.

content.title: Content
content.description: SKILL.md as written, front matter included.

SkillDetailRecord.title: SkillDetailRecord
SkillDetailRecord.description: One skill with the whole text of its ``SKILL.md``.

bytes.title: Bytes
bytes.description: The file's size in UTF-8 bytes.

SkillFileRecord.title: SkillFileRecord
SkillFileRecord.description: One file of a skill: its path within the skill, size and digest.

path.title: Path
path.description: The file the finding is about, relative to the skill; null for the skill as a whole.

SkillFindingRecord.title: SkillFindingRecord
SkillFindingRecord.description: One thing a check found in a skill.

SkillListResponse.title: SkillListResponse
SkillListResponse.description: Every skill of the package, ordered by name, and the set's revision.

applies_when.title: Applies When
applies_when.description: The skill's parsed selection predicate, without the keys it leaves unset; null when it declares none.

files.title: Files
files.description: Every file of the skill, SKILL.md included, in path order.

SkillRecord.title: SkillRecord
SkillRecord.description: One skill: what it is, when it applies, and the files it is made of.

SkillRefusalDetail.title: SkillRefusalDetail
SkillRefusalDetail.description:
Why a skill verb was refused, or why a message's skills were.

``skill_not_found``: no skill of the package, or of the run, has the name.
``skills_invalid``: a message's skill list repeats a name, names more than
eight, or names one not of the form ``cadrumo-<lowercase words>``.
``skills_unavailable``: the run was accepted with no skill to give.

SkillRefusalResponse.title: SkillRefusalResponse
SkillRefusalResponse.description: The body served for a refused skill verb or skill list.

SkillVerificationRecord.title: SkillVerificationRecord
SkillVerificationRecord.description: What checking one skill found; ``valid`` is false if any finding is an error.

SkillVerifyOneRequest.title: SkillVerifyOneRequest
SkillVerifyOneRequest.description: Check one skill; the body is empty.

SkillVerifyRequest.title: SkillVerifyRequest
SkillVerifyRequest.description:
Check the named skills, or every skill when ``names`` is left out.

``names`` holds at most :data:`MAX_VERIFIED_SKILLS` distinct names, each no
wider than the widest name a skill can have; a list past either bound, or
one that repeats a name, is refused before any skill is checked.

SkillVerifyResponse.title: SkillVerifyResponse
SkillVerifyResponse.description: The checks of the skills asked for, in the order asked, and the revision.

SkipReason.title: SkipReason
SkipReason.description: Why an entry of a conversation's store is not listed as an attachment.

SkippedAttachmentEntry.title: SkippedAttachmentEntry
SkippedAttachmentEntry.description: An entry of a conversation's store that is not an attachment.

StatusFailure.title: StatusFailure
StatusFailure.description: The last refresh that failed, kept beside the last value read.

StatusFailureKind.title: StatusFailureKind
StatusFailureKind.description: Why the last status refresh failed.

StatusIncident.title: StatusIncident
StatusIncident.description: A recent incident a vendor's feed lists, for display.

StatusKind.title: StatusKind
StatusKind.description:
How a provider publishes its service status, which selects its reader.

Values:
    STATUSPAGE_V2: A statuspage-style JSON API with components.
    RSS: An incident feed, which states no component state.
    NONE: Nothing machine-readable; status is always unknown.

StatusSource.title: StatusSource
StatusSource.description:
Where a provider publishes its service status.

Attributes:
    kind: How it is published, which selects the reader.
    page_url: The page a person reads, or null where there is none.
    api_url: The machine-readable endpoint the reader polls; null exactly
        when ``kind`` is ``none``.

SubagentSnapshot.title: SubagentSnapshot
SubagentSnapshot.description:
A subagent of the run's agent: activity nested under one tool call.

Its own tool calls are the run's tool calls that name it.

SubagentState.title: SubagentState
SubagentState.description:
What a subagent of the run's agent is doing, as its lane reports it.

``requires_action`` is a child parked on a permission request; ``idle`` is a
child whose turn ended and that its lane may still address again.

ThreadMetadata.title: ThreadMetadata
ThreadMetadata.description: Provenance and context attached to a run.

checkpoint_parent_id.title: Checkpoint Parent Id
checkpoint_parent_id.description: The parent the current checkpoint records. It may name a checkpoint that no longer exists: once a run settles, its superseded history is pruned and only this reference to it remains. Do not read it as a checkpoint that can be fetched.

history_depth.title: History Depth
history_depth.description: How deep the current checkpoint's recorded ancestry goes: 2 when it names a parent, 1 when it is the first of its thread, null when no checkpoint was read. Recorded ancestry, not stored rows - a settled run's history is pruned and its depth does not fall.

ThreadStateSnapshot.title: ThreadStateSnapshot
ThreadStateSnapshot.description:
Complete thread state for reattaching to a run's event stream.

The client fetches this via REST, notes ``last_sequence``, then discards any
streamed frame with ``sequence <= last_sequence``.

ThreadStatus.title: ThreadStatus
ThreadStatus.description: Durable lifecycle states for a run.

ToolCallContentDiff.title: ToolCallContentDiff
ToolCallContentDiff.description: Diff content block within a tool call.

ToolCallContentTerminal.title: ToolCallContentTerminal
ToolCallContentTerminal.description: Terminal output content block within a tool call.

ToolCallContentText.title: ToolCallContentText
ToolCallContentText.description: Plain text content block within a tool call.

ToolCallLocation.title: ToolCallLocation
ToolCallLocation.description: File location associated with a tool call.

tool_server.title: Tool Server
tool_server.description: The tool server that owns the tool, read from the identity its provider named the call by, e.g. 'cadrumo' or 'cadrumo_agent_tools'. Null for a tool the provider carries in itself.

tool_name.title: Tool Name
tool_name.description: The tool's own name within its server, e.g. 'authority' or 'load_skill'; for a tool the provider carries in itself, the provider's name for it.

tool_reach.description: How far the tool reaches: 'local_read' reads this machine, 'local_write' may change it, 'online' may reach beyond it. Null when it is not known.

failure.description: Why the call failed; null on a call that did not fail, and on a failed call that stated no reason.

ToolCallSnapshot.title: ToolCallSnapshot
ToolCallSnapshot.description: Fully materialized tool call (all incremental updates merged).

ToolCallStatus.title: ToolCallStatus
ToolCallStatus.description: Lifecycle states for a single tool invocation.

code.title: Code
code.description: The closed refusal code the tool's typed result stated, lowercase letters, digits, '_' and '.'. Absent when it stated none.

recovery_action_id.title: Recovery Action Id
recovery_action_id.description: The operator action that recovers from the refusal, when the tool's result named one. Present only with a code.

message.title: Message
message.description: The first line of the tool result's error text, trimmed to at most 300 characters, so a person can read why the call failed. Absent when the result gave no readable line.

ToolFailure.title: ToolFailure
ToolFailure.description:
Why a tool call failed: the refusal it stated and the reason it gave.

Every field is ``None`` when the call stated nothing of it. The result's
other content is never part of it.

ToolReach.title: ToolReach
ToolReach.description:
How far a tool reaches when it is called.

``local_read`` tools read what is on this machine and change nothing,
``local_write`` tools may change it, and ``online`` tools may reach beyond
it. A call whose reach is not known is served without one rather than as any
of these.

TranscriptAvailability.title: TranscriptAvailability
TranscriptAvailability.description:
Why a run's conversation is, or is not, readable from its checkpoint.

A run's transcript lives only in the checkpoint, so an unread checkpoint
yields an empty message list that is indistinguishable from a run that
genuinely said nothing. This classification is what tells the two apart, and
it exists so no reader has to infer loss from an empty list.

``NOT_YET_RECORDED`` is the only non-fault absence: the run has not been
dispatched, so there is nothing to have lost. ``MISSING`` and ``UNREADABLE``
are both faults and differ in whether the checkpoint is gone or merely
unreachable right now.

A run whose transcript was deliberately released under a retention policy
would be a fourth, non-fault member. It is deliberately absent: no
production seam prunes a checkpoint today, so every absence really is a
fault, and a member with no producer would let a genuine loss be dismissed
as intended.

UnreadSource.title: UnreadSource
UnreadSource.description:
A source the compile meant to read for a lane and did not.

A lane whose vendor listing was not read is served from the next source in
precedence, and this record says so, so the lane is never mistaken for one
the vendor's own listing answered for.

Attributes:
    source: The id of the unread source in the document's sources.
    reason: Why it was not read. It names a setting, never a credential value.

WorkerConnectionStatus.title: WorkerConnectionStatus
WorkerConnectionStatus.description:
What the watchdog last observed about the worker process it supervises.

``PENDING`` is the pre-observation value the state container is created
with: a watchdog exists but has not yet completed a probe, which is not the
same claim as ``DOWN``. ``UP`` and ``DOWN`` are settled observations,
``RESTARTING`` is the window in which the watchdog is deliberately replacing
the process, and ``UNKNOWN`` is what a reader gets when no worker state
container exists at all - a gateway configured without a supervised worker.

WorkerLifecycleState.title: WorkerLifecycleState
WorkerLifecycleState.description:
The gateway-owned worker's rung on the cold-to-execution ladder.

``cold`` is the pre-demand resting state: no worker exists yet and one is
startable on first execution demand. It is informational, never degradation.
``starting`` is the single-flight startup window, ``ready`` is an up and
reachable worker, and ``unavailable`` is a worker that started but is down or
restarting after demand.

GatewayServiceToken.description: Gateway service token. The service publishes it in an owner-restricted `service.token` handoff file adjacent to the `service.json` discovery record, whose `handoff_reference` names that file without embedding the secret. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
